title: The Remix Era (Hip-Hop Soul)
theme: The 1990s movement that merged hard hip-hop drum breaks with smooth R&B vocals, defining the sound of New York and transforming R&B radio forever.
narrativePurpose: Test players on the iconic features, production teams, and sample origins that defined the golden era of the R&B/Hip-Hop crossover remix.
toneProgression: Massive rap features on R&B hits → The producers and sample crate-diggers behind the boards → Obscure remixes and underground hip-hop crossovers

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The massive crossovers that took R&B to the block. Identify the iconic rap features and the definitive hip-hop soul anthems.

questions.question: Which R&B group dominated hip-hop soul radio in 1996 with the Dr. Dre-featuring smash 'No Diggity'?

metadata.fact: 'No Diggity' spent three weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996 and won the Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group — Blackstreet's commercial peak and one of the defining hip-hop soul records of the decade.
metadata.storyHook: Puff Daddy brought a rugged, unpredictable hip-hop energy to the biggest pop star in the world, changing radio formats forever.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Columbia). ASCAP database confirms Russell Jones as co-writer. MTV retrospective interviews.

questions.question: Which legendary female MC opened the iconic hip-hop remix of Brandy's 'I Wanna Be Down'?

metadata.fact: The groundbreaking remix featured MC Lyte, Yo-Yo, and Queen Latifah, creating a definitive female empowerment anthem.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Atlantic). ASCAP database confirms Lana Moorer. Historic Billboard reporting.

sources.title: I Wanna Be Down (Human Rhythm Hip Hop Remix) – Discogs

questions.question: The Notorious B.I.G. and which rising Bad Boy rapper provided the massive guest verses on the remix of 112's 'Only You'?

metadata.fact: The 'Only You' remix officially introduced Mase to a mainstream audience, launching his blockbuster Bad Boy career.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Bad Boy/Arista). ASCAP database confirms Mason Betha. Documentaries on Bad Boy Records.

questions.question: SWV — whose 1993 'Right Here (Human Nature Remix)' became a hip-hop soul landmark — is an acronym standing for what?

metadata.fact: SWV — Sisters With Voices — formed in New York City in 1988. The trio of Coko, Lelee, and Taj became one of the defining acts of the hip-hop soul era.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (RCA). ASCAP sample clearance records. Teddy Riley interviews.

questions.question: Mariah Carey's 1996 hip-hop soul ballad 'Breakdown' featured which Ohio rap trio?

metadata.fact: 'Breakdown' from Mariah's Daydream album featured Bone Thugs-n-Harmony — an unexpected but seamless pairing that demonstrated how fully hip-hop and R&B had merged by 1996.
metadata.sourceNotes: Grammy Awards historical database. Official CD single liner notes (Def Jam).

questions.question: The Notorious B.I.G. featured on the Bad Boy debut single of which female R&B trio — the track that introduced them to mainstream audiences in 1995?

metadata.fact: 'Can't You See' debuted on the New Jersey Drive Vol. 1 soundtrack in 1995 — Total's introduction to mainstream audiences and one of Bad Boy's earliest hip-hop soul crossover moments.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (LaFace). Billboard chart archives.

questions.question: Which rapper — known as 'The Overweight Lover' — was the flagship hip-hop artist at Uptown Records alongside Mary J. Blige?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — UPTOWN RECORDS HIP-HOP FLAGSHIP ARTIST

metadata.fact: Heavy D was the commercial anchor of Uptown Records before Mary J. Blige arrived — his success gave Andre Harrell the credibility and budget to develop the hip-hop soul sound that defined the label.
metadata.sourceNotes: RIAA certification database. Official Uptown Records release history.

reserve.question: Which female R&B trio broke through in 1994 with the Denzil Foster-produced hip-hop soul ballad 'If You Love Me'?

metadata.fact: Brownstone's 'If You Love Me' — produced by Denzil Foster and Thomas McElroy — became one of 1994's defining slow jam crossover records, reaching #8 on the Billboard Hot 100.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Mercury). ASCAP database confirms Melissa Elliott.

sources.title: If You Love Me (Brownstone song) – Wikipedia

reserve.question: Kelly Price's massive 'Friend of Mine' remix featured R. Kelly alongside which legendary soul singer?

metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Island Black Music). ASCAP database confirms Ronald Isley.

sources.title: Friend of Mine (Kelly Price song) – Wikipedia

reserve.question: Xscape's hip-hop soul debut — which launched the Jermaine Dupri-produced group in 1993 — was titled what?

metadata.fact: Xscape's debut album Hummin' Comin' at 'Cha (1993) was produced by Jermaine Dupri and introduced the Atlanta quartet as one of So So Def's flagship hip-hop soul acts.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Bad Boy/Arista). ASCAP database confirms Inga Marchand.

reserve.question: Horace Brown's 1996 'One for the Money' remix prominently featured an early guest verse from which rap mogul?

metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Motown). ASCAP database confirms Shawn Carter.

sources.title: One for the Money (Horace Brown song) – Discogs

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: The producers behind the boards and the obscure features that made the hip-hop soul era undeniable.

questions.question: Which NYC-based production duo, known collectively as the Trackmasters, dominated the R&B remix era for artists like Mariah Carey and Mary J. Blige?

metadata.fact: Jean-Claude 'Poke' Olivier and Samuel 'Tone' Barnes (The Trackmasters) were the defining architects of the glossy 90s hip-hop soul remix sound.
metadata.sourceNotes: ASCAP/BMI databases confirming Olivier and Barnes. Numerous historical producer credits.

questions.question: Jodeci's 'Freek'n You' received a gritty 'Mr. Dalvin's Freek Mix' featuring which two members of the Wu-Tang Clan?

metadata.album: The Show, the After Party, the Hotel
metadata.fact: The rugged remix became a massive street anthem, proving that Jodeci's sound could seamlessly integrate with the hardest NYC hip-hop.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Uptown/MCA). ASCAP database. Wu-Tang discography archives.

questions.question: Janet Jackson's 'Got 'til It's Gone' received the legendary 'Ummah Jay Dee's Revenge Mix', produced by which Detroit hip-hop icon?

metadata.song: Got 'til It's Gone (Ummah Jay Dee's Revenge Mix)
metadata.fact: J Dilla (then known as Jay Dee) crafted the official remix under his Ummah production collective moniker.
metadata.storyHook: The velvet rope opened up to allow one of underground hip-hop's most revered beatmakers to touch a pop masterpiece.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official 12-inch single credits (Virgin). J Dilla discography archives. ASCAP publishing records.

questions.question: The 'Hip Hop Mix' of Boyz II Men's 'Vibin'' featured Craig Mack, Busta Rhymes, Method Man, and which Naughty By Nature frontman?

metadata.fact: The 'New Flava' mix was a posse-cut remix that successfully bridged the gap between smooth Philadelphia harmony and rugged East Coast rap.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD single credits (Motown). ASCAP database confirms Anthony Criss (Treach).

questions.question: Next's massive 1998 hit 'Too Close' was built around the groove from 'Christmas Rappin'' by which hip-hop pioneer?

metadata.fact: Producer Kay Gee looped Kurtis Blow's 1979 classic 'Christmas Rappin'' to create the instrumental for 'Too Close'.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Too Close' samples/interpolates 'Christmas Rappin'' by Kurtis Blow. Sources: WhoSampled https://www.whosampled.com/sample/911/Next-Too-Close-Kurtis-Blow-Christmas-Rappin/, Songfacts https://www.songfacts.com/facts/next/too-close, https://www.songfacts.com/facts/kurtis-blow/christmas-rappin. Note: produced by Kay Gee (Naughty by Nature) — EP017 production credit is consistent with this sample credit.

questions.question: P. Diddy celebrated his label's dominance of the hip-hop soul era with the compilation 'We Invented the Remix' in what year?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE YEAR BAD BOY INVENTED THE REMIX

metadata.artist: P. Diddy & The Bad Boy Family
metadata.fact: The album debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200, proving that Bad Boy's signature remix formula was still highly profitable in the 2000s.
metadata.sourceNotes: RIAA certification database. Official Billboard 200 chart archives.

reserve.question: Faith Evans' 1998 anthem 'Love Like This' was built on a massive loop of 'Chic Cheer' by which legendary 70s band?

metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD liner notes for Keep the Faith (Bad Boy). ASCAP database confirms Nile Rodgers & Bernard Edwards.

sources.title: Love Like This (Faith Evans song) – Wikipedia

reserve.question: Blackstreet's iconic 'No Diggity' famously sampled 'Grandma's Hands' by which soul legend?

metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD liner notes for Another Level (Interscope). ASCAP database confirms Bill Withers.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: The deepest hip-hop soul crate digging. Test your knowledge of obscure samples, uncredited producers, and underground remixes.

questions.question: D'Angelo's 'Brown Sugar' received a gritty, underground hip-hop remix produced by which legendary Gang Starr member?

metadata.fact: DJ Premier's remix stripped away the lush neo-soul instrumentation, placing D'Angelo's vocals over a raw, signature boom-bap beat.
metadata.storyHook: When neo-soul needed street credibility in New York, they called the greatest hip-hop producer in the city.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official 12-inch vinyl credits (EMI). Discogs release database. DJ Premier discography records.

questions.question: Mary J. Blige's 'Love No Limit' Puff Daddy remix famously anchored its groove on a sample of 'Risin' to the Top' by which 80s artist?

metadata.fact: Keni Burke's 1982 bassline from 'Risin' to the Top' is one of the most sampled grooves in hip-hop and R&B history.
metadata.storyHook: Puff Daddy didn't just remix the song, he changed the underlying DNA by adding one of the most recognizable basslines of the 80s.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD liner notes for What's the 411? Remix (Uptown). ASCAP database clearance records.

sources.title: Risin' to the Top by Keni Burke – WhoSampled

questions.question: In what year did Mary J. Blige transition out of the heavy hip-hop soul era with her landmark album 'No More Drama'?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — THE YEAR THE DRAMA ENDED

metadata.fact: Released in August 2001, the album marked a significant lyrical and sonic evolution for the Queen of Hip-Hop Soul.
metadata.sourceNotes: RIAA database. Official MCA Records release history.

reserve.question: Timbaland's production on Ginuwine's debut 'Pony' defined the hip-hop soul sound for 1997 — what was that debut album titled?

metadata.fact: Ginuwine...the Bachelor (1997) was produced almost entirely by Timbaland — its futuristic drum programming and minimalist hip-hop soul arrangements established a new aesthetic that influenced a decade of R&B production.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official 12-inch single credits (Arista). ASCAP database confirms James Todd Smith.

reserve.question: Michael Jackson's 'Remember The Time' received a house/R&B 'Silky Soul 7' remix produced by which Chicago house pioneer?

metadata.sourceNotes: Official 12-inch single credits (Epic). Discogs release database.
